summary.one_liner: Wikipedia encyclopedia article describing file sharing: the history, types (peer-to-peer, cloud sync, private, academic), economic impact and copyright issues of distributing digital files.

summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software product. It covers how file sharing works, from removable media and FTP to Usenet, Napster, Gnutella, BitTorrent and cloud sync services. It describes the main types of file sharing: peer-to-peer, cloud-based sync and sharing, private organizational sharing, and academic sharing. It also summarizes economic studies on whether file sharing hurts music sales, and copyright lawsuits such as MGM v. Grokster.
notable: Covers file sharing history from 1970s FTP and Usenet through Napster, Gnutella, Kazaa and BitTorrent
Summarizes conflicting economic studies on music file sharing and sales
Lists related topics such as comparison of file-sharing applications and warez
caveats: Describes historical shutdowns and lawsuits; some services mentioned no longer operate
Covers legal and contested claims; the page itself notes some studies are disputed
